reason: Both debates converge on calm-first, one-at-a-time reintroduction, red flags and a written log, and both narrow claims under objection. B spends its turns on the mechanics of finding the cause: the cost of each retest, expectation bias in reading a patch test, and barrier-stacking as a cause no single test can catch. A spends two turns guessing at the user's motive (money) and then retracting the guess. B's ending also gives the user more conditions they can actually check.

comparisons.a_observation: The Subtractor invents a motive (the user paid for the products and wants to save the routine), and the Skeptic spends the next turn rejecting it because nothing in the user's words mentions money. Earlier, A.debate[3].text does narrow the plan well (test pairs because joint causes hide from single tests).
comparisons.b_observation: The Subtractor points to the real cost of each reintroduction. The Experimenter concedes that testing everything is greedy, but names the opposite risk (dropping a harmless product and keeping the guilty one) and narrows to prioritized small-patch trials. The Skeptic then attacks the trial itself through expectation bias and proposes writing down in advance what counts as a reaction.
comparisons.why_it_matters: The user asked how to find the cause. B's exchanges each improve the method the user will run. A's motive detour mostly cancels itself out.

comparisons.a_observation: Gives clear red flags, a calm-first step, a logged one-at-a-time reintroduction with pairs tested last, the option of simply dropping nonessential products, and dermatologist patch testing.
comparisons.b_observation: Gives red flags, prioritized reintroduction starting with the most valued product on a small area, and an observable check A lacks: if stinging continues a week or two after stopping all three, the cause is probably something else. It also suggests using fewer products at once if the reaction appears only when layering.
comparisons.why_it_matters: The 'persists after stopping' condition tells the user whether the product hypothesis survives at all, before any reintroduction starts.

comparisons.a_observation: Explicitly marks the mind's own extensions beyond the book ('my own addition to Taleb', 'go further than Taleb').
comparisons.b_observation: Lists the products, severity and other changes as unknowns. It also lists 'whether they were introduced together' as unknown, although the user's wording ('started three new skincare products last week') largely answers that.
comparisons.why_it_matters: A keeps the book's idea separate from the mind's extension more visibly. This is a smaller advantage that does not outweigh B's stronger interaction.

best_of_a.observation: The Controlled Tester takes the Skeptic's point that products may only irritate together and narrows his own method: test singly, then in pairs, and admit that joint causes are its weakest case.

best_of_b.observation: The Skeptic warns that expecting a product to be guilty can make a faint tingle feel like proof, and proposes writing down beforehand what counts as a reaction, along with the date, weather and other changes.

concerns.description: Speculates about a financial motive the user never stated. The next turn walks it back, but it still steers the self-reflection in A.clearer.
Treats whether the products were introduced together as unknown, although the user's wording implies they were started at roughly the same time.
